report.note: Two fixed epochs; validation loss is not meaning preservation or style quality. Test split untouched by optimization and evaluation.

diagnostics.limitations: Exact textual differences measure responsiveness, not stylistic quality. Identical output can be appropriate for some inputs. One deterministic generation per condition.

semantic_summary.reviewer: assistant editorial review, unblinded; not independent human evaluation
semantic_summary.summary: Five clear meaning failures and three possible completion/intent shifts were found across 150 after-training outputs. Style remains weak; this adapter is not deployed.

rubric.0: Changed or omitted claim, role, attribution or stance

style_findings: At level 0/25 the nickname case correctly changes Dumocrats to Democrats; high levels retain it.
The criticism case starting with Democrats does not acquire the observed nickname at high levels.
The no-layoffs case uses a rhetorical question at 50/75/100 while preserving both time qualifications.
Many other changes are punctuation, capitalization or ordinary paraphrase, not distinctive learned style.
16/30 cases are identical across all five levels; no general monotonic style control established.
semantic_summary.limitations: Single deterministic sample per condition. All after outputs were reviewed; before outputs were spot reviewed, so no before/after semantic accuracy comparison is claimed. Existing development cases are not an unseen benchmark.

deployment: Experimental adapter only; live 9B slider unchanged.
